title: Image model choices keep up with the API
summary:
Image models are easier to find, text responses are more predictable, and feeds and redirects got stricter about what they pass along.

The image feed editor now fetches its model options from the image API, so newly available models can appear without a frontend change. The selector has a loading state and falls back to its previous list if the request fails. The model list also gives the Cloudflare-hosted DeepSeek distill model a distinct name, `deepseek-reasoning-qwen`, instead of colliding with the full DeepSeek R1 entry.

Most text models gained a Llama 4-derived conversational prompt while purpose-specific models retain their own instructions. POST text requests now use the entire body for cache keys, so changing a parameter such as `seed` no longer retrieves a response cached for different parameters.

The image service now marks feed events whose prompts match mature terms. Feed listeners filter both replayed and new results for mature and other restricted content, regardless of the `nsfw` query parameter.
